matterOverview.title: Rajesh Kumar vs. Suresh Traders — Cheque Bounce Dispute

factsSummary: The plaintiff issued a loan of INR 5,00,000 to the defendant in January 2025. The defendant issued a post-dated cheque for repayment, which was presented on 10 March 2025 and returned dishonoured with the memo 'Insufficient Funds'. A legal notice under Section 138 of the NI Act was sent on 25 March 2025. The defendant failed to make payment within the statutory 15-day period.
applicableProvisions: Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881
Section 139 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 — Presumption in favour of holder

precedents.title: Kumar vs. Naveen Chand (2022)
precedents.summary: Cheque bounce case where the Supreme Court held that once the signature and issuance are admitted, the presumption under Section 139 operates in favour of the holder.

precedents.title: Rangappa vs. Sri Mohan (2010)
precedents.summary: Landmark judgment establishing that the presumption under Section 139 is a rebuttable presumption and the accused must show a probable defence.

matterOverview.title: Priya Sharma vs. HomeGlad Appliances — Consumer Complaint
matterOverview.jurisdiction: District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum, Mumbai

factsSummary: The complainant purchased a washing machine from HomeGlad Appliances for INR 38,000 on 15 January 2025. The product developed a major defect within 15 days of purchase. Despite multiple complaints to the service centre, no resolution was provided for over 45 days. The complainant sent a legal notice on 20 February 2025 seeking replacement or refund, which was ignored.
applicableProvisions: Section 2(1)(g) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 — Defect in goods
Section 49 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 — Right to replacement/refund

precedents.title: M/S Sonic Electrochem vs. Ravi Sharma (2023)
precedents.summary: Consumer complaint where the commission held that repeated defects within warranty period entitle the consumer to full replacement or refund.

precedents.title: LG Electronics vs. Shashi Bala (2021)
precedents.summary: Case establishing that manufacturers cannot limit their liability for manufacturing defects through warranty terms.

favorableFactors: Manufacturer failed to respond to legal notice

simulationFeedback.weakestPoint: No independent expert inspection report to corroborate defect

matterOverview.title: Amit Verma vs. TechCore Solutions — Wrongful Termination

factsSummary: The claimant was employed as a Senior Software Engineer at TechCore Solutions since January 2022. On 5 April 2025, the claimant was terminated without any prior notice or warning. The employer cited 'performance issues' but failed to provide any performance improvement plan (PIP) or documented evidence of poor performance. The claimant had a clean service record with consistently positive appraisals.
applicableProvisions: Section 25-F of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 — Conditions precedent to retrenchment
Section 2(oo) of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 — Definition of retrenchment

precedents.title: D.K. Yadav vs. J.M.A. Industries (1993)
precedents.summary: Landmark case establishing that termination without notice and opportunity of hearing violates principles of natural justice and Section 25-F of the Industrial Disputes Act.

precedents.title: Rajasthan State Road Transport Corp. vs. Shyam Bihari (2022)
precedents.summary: Recent judgment reiterating that termination without complying with Section 25-F is void ab initio, even if the employee was a probationer.
